threatModelSummary: Read-only, unauthenticated feature: an offline Cesium globe view at /reagent-map (behind a build-time-only feature flag, default off) renders site data fetched once from GET /api/reagent-sites. No forms, no auth, no write paths, no PII. The only new attack surface is (1) a dev-only Vite middleware serving Cesium's static assets from node_modules, and (2) a new pinned dependency (cesium@1.146.0). Both were inspected directly; no Critical or High findings. The one prior Critical-class issue in this feature — a WebGL context leak when fetchReagentSites() rejected after buildViewer() resolved — was already found by code-reviewer and fixed by the developer (Promise.allSettled + explicit destroy()-on-failure); verified correct by reading the current code, not relied on secondhand.
dependencyAudit: pnpm audit --prod run against the full workspace: 33 findings (2 low, 15 moderate, 14 high, 2 critical), all under apps__mock-api>express (qs, body-parser) — pre-existing transitive advisories unrelated to this feature's files_touched scope (mock-api's package.json was not modified by reagent-map-globe).
cesium@1.146.0 (new, pinned exact version, no caret range): zero advisories reported by pnpm audit for this package.

stride.assessed: No authentication or identity on this route; it is a public, read-only view with no session or token handling introduced. No spoofing surface — nothing to impersonate.

Site data (id/name/lat/lng) comes from the same-origin mock API, not user input, and is rendered via Vue's auto-escaping `{{ site.name }}` interpolation (no v-html) — no injection path. The feature flag (VITE_FEATURE_REAGENT_MAP) is a build-time constant baked into the bundle via import.meta.env, not a runtime-mutable value a client request could flip.
No state-changing action exists in this feature (view-only), so there is nothing a user could perform and later deny. No audit trail gap applicable.

Checked what can be read: site names/coordinates are non-sensitive seed data, already served by the pre-existing reagent-sites-api with no auth gate (out of scope here). Checked what can carry it out: the new dev-only cesiumStaticAssetsPlugin in vite.config.ts is a path-traversal candidate — verified safe (see findings). window.__SATURDAY_CESIUM__ exposes only the Viewer/Cesium handle for the Playwright test seam, no credentials or secrets attached.

fetchReagentSites() has an explicit 5s AbortController timeout (no unbounded network call). The previously-found WebGL-context-leak-on-partial-failure (repeated failed mounts exhausting the browser's per-page WebGL context limit) was fixed in this round via Promise.allSettled + newViewer.destroy() on a sites-fetch rejection — verified by reading the current onMounted implementation at ReagentMapView.vue:119-138; both rejection branches are handled and nothing is left orphaned.
No roles, permissions, or per-user data in this feature — every visitor sees the same fixed site list. No privilege boundary exists for this view to cross.

findings.title: cesiumStaticAssetsPlugin's resolveRequestedFile can throw on malformed percent-encoding
findings.description: resolveRequestedFile calls decodeURIComponent(urlPath.slice(...)) with no try/catch. A request like `/cesium/%` is invalid percent-encoding and decodeURIComponent throws a URIError synchronously inside the middleware, uncaught. The path-traversal guard itself is correct — decode-then-normalize ordering is right, the '..'-prefix check after normalize correctly rejects traversal attempts (e.g. '../../etc/passwd', '..%2f..%2fetc%2fpasswd'), and path.join's semantics mean an absolute-looking segment like '/etc/passwd' gets appended under CESIUM_SOURCE_DIR rather than escaping it, as path.resolve would allow. The only gap is the unhandled throw on bad encoding. Blast radius is minimal: this middleware only runs in `configureServer` (vite dev server, not shipped to production or dist/), and the dev server binds to localhost by default with no `host` change in this diff — so exploitation requires a request already on the loopback interface, which already has full filesystem access.
findings.verification: Not applicable — Low severity per the severity table (track as tech debt), no fix required before QA. If QA wants to exercise it: request `GET /cesium/%` while the dev server is running and confirm whether the dev server process surfaces a clean 500/next() vs crashing; expected is Vite/connect's middleware dispatcher catching the throw, but this was not executed, only read.
